facts: The common cold is a viral infection of your nose and throat (upper respiratory tract).
Most people recover from a common cold in a week or 10 days.
Symptoms might last longer in people who smoke.
prevention: Wash your hands often with soap and water.
Avoid close contact with anyone who has a cold.

facts: Influenza is a viral infection that attacks your respiratory system.
Flu is primarily treated with rest and fluids to allow the body to fight the infection on its own.
Annual flu vaccines can help prevent the flu and its complications.
prevention: Annual vaccination is the most effective way to prevent the flu.
Cover your mouth and nose when coughing or sneezing.

facts: A migraine is a headache that can cause severe throbbing pain or a pulsing sensation.
It's often accompanied by nausea, vomiting, and extreme sensitivity to light and sound.
Migraine attacks can last for hours to days.
treatment_tips: Resting in a quiet, dark room can help.
Hot or cold compresses to your head or neck may provide relief.

facts: Dehydration occurs when you use or lose more fluid than you take in.
If you don't replace lost fluids, you will get dehydrated.
Anyone can become dehydrated, but the condition is especially dangerous for young children and older adults.
rehydration: Drink plenty of fluids, and focus on water or drinks with electrolytes.
Avoid caffeine and alcohol which can increase dehydration.
